Mass Slides Builder Build 41 · 23 September 2026

Paste this Sunday's texts, press Build, and you get the complete Order of Mass as a PowerPoint file. Text is grown to fill each slide. Every part takes as many hymns as you like, a blank line starts a new slide, and each part's lines-per-slide and font size can be set on its own. Type a hymn's chorus once in its own box and it is repeated after every verse. The part's name sits as one small line at the very top, so the text still has the whole slide. Where a part can be sung or recited — Gloria, Creed, Our Father, Sanctus, Agnus Dei — the recited text stays in the deck but hides itself as soon as you paste a song. Nothing leaves your computer.

Put the part's name on a line of its own, then the song under it.
A blank line starts a new slide; a new page or slide in a PDF or
PowerPoint does the same.

Names it knows: Entrance · Penitential Act · Kyrie / Lord Have Mercy ·
Gloria · Creed · Prayer of the Faithful · Offertory · Thanksgiving ·
Consecration · Sanctus / Holy Holy · Mystery of Faith · Our Father ·
Agnus Dei / Lamb of God · Communion · Post-Communion · Recessional ·
Announcements

Build

The middle projector, the Acer, cuts the first and last letter off each line. The other two are fine, so the file is not at fault — that projector is throwing away its own edges. This margin keeps the words clear of the edge on all three until it is put right.

To put it right:

1. Swap that projector's receiver box with one from a projector that is fine. If the cropping stays with the Acer it is the projector; if it moves, it is the box.

2. On the Acer: Menu → Image → HDMI Scan Info → Underscan, and Image → Aspect Ratio → Auto.

3. If it is the box, match its output resolution to the projector's own.

When a whole line shows on all three, set this back to "Text right to the edge" for the biggest text.
